annual base rate filing consisting of a 0.61% 
increase to be effective with bills rendered on 
and after November 1, 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Order entered: 
 
 
ORDER APPROVING ANNUAL BASE RATE FILING 
I. 
INTRODUCTION 
 
This case involves the annual base rate filing that Vermont Gas Systems, Inc. (“VGS”) is 
required to file with the Vermont Public Utility Commission (“Commission”) pursuant to 
Paragraph 3 of VGS’s current Alternative Regulation Plan (the “Plan”).1  As discussed below, 
the Commission concludes that the base rate filing is consistent with the requirements of the Plan 
and therefore approves VGS’s requested 0.61% base rate increase, a $465,764 increase to VGS’s 
revenue requirement, effective with bills rendered on or after November 1, 2026. 
II. 
PROCEDURAL HISTORY 
 
On August 18, 2023, the Commission approved the Plan in Case No. 22-5085-PET. 
 
On June 30, 2026, VGS filed its annual base rate adjustment in this case.  VGS’s filing 
was supported by revised tariff sheets and several attachments detailing the data and cost-of-
service information that was used by VGS to calculate its proposed base rate adjustment.   
 
On July 15, 2026, the Vermont Department of Public Service (“Department”) filed a 
recommendation on the proposed base rate increase (“Department Recommendation”).  The 
Department states that it “has identified no financial or procedural grounds necessitating an 
investigation under 30 V.S.A. §225” and that the “structure of the [fiscal year] 2027 filing 
strictly adheres to the formulaic approach established in the [Plan].”2  The Department

III. 
BASE RATE ADJUSTMENT PROVISIONS UNDER THE PLAN 
 
Paragraph 3 of the Plan sets out a formulaic and mechanical process that VGS must 
follow to make its annual base rate adjustments over the term of the Plan.  For VGS’s 2027 
annual base rate adjustment, Paragraph 3(c)(iv) of the Plan establishes that the annual base rate 
adjustment must: 
be set based on (1) Operating Costs as adjusted by the Indexed Market Adjustment 
and any Additional Innovation Expense, if applicable, and (2) Non-Operating 
Costs, pursuant to a fixed 1-year Rate Base Plan for the [2027] extension period . . . 
as adjusted by Additional Innovation Capital, if applicable.  
 
Operating Costs are defined under the Plan to include “all costs categorized as operating 
costs under VGS’s non-gas Cost of Service for FY2024, which includes Production, 
Transmission, Distribution, Customer Accounts, Sales, Admin & General, and Other Income.”3  
The “Indexed Market Adjustment” is pegged to changes in inflation as determined by 
fluctuations in the Consumer Price Index and the U.S. Bureau of Labor & Statistics Employment 
Cost Index.  The Plan also establishes that changes in Operating Costs “shall be no higher than 
4% and no lower than 2%.”4 
 
Non-Operating Costs include taxes, cost to finance rate base, and depreciation.5  VGS’s 
Non-Operating Costs can be adjusted based on changes to its property tax rates.  VGS is also 
required to adjust the cost to finance its rate base annually.  The Plan fixes VGS’s debt-to-equity 
ratio at 50%/50%,6 but VGS’s authorized rate of return on equity must be adjusted annually 
based on fluctuations in the yield on the 10-year Treasury Note.7  Any changes to VGS’s short- 
or long-term debt rates also flow through the annual base rate adjustments.

IV. 
DISCUSSION 
 
VGS requests that the Commission approve a 0.61% base rate increase as calculated by 
following the base rate adjustment mechanisms included in Paragraph 3 of the Plan.  With 
respect to the overall 0.61% increase, VGS clarifies that the total adjustment is the net effect of 
the following components: 
• A 2.51% increase based on VGS’s fiscal year 2027 capital investment additions that are 
fixed in VGS’s one-year rate base plan, which was approved by the Commission in Case 
No. 25-1106-PET; 
• A 1.84% increase attributable to the formulaic change in operating expenses based on the 
Consumer Price Index and Bureau of Labor Statistics index as set forth in the Plan; 
• A 0.02% increase based on the formulaic adjustment to VGS’s authorized rate of return 
on equity, which resulted in a change from 9.62% to 9.63%; 
• A 3.64% decrease due to the completion of the Rate Smoothing Adjuster, which was 
fully returned to customers in 2026;8 and 
• VGS previously returned the full System Expansion and Reliability Fund (“SERF”) 
balance to customers, but there is a small balance associated with timing differences and 
interest, which VGS proposes to return to customers with this filing, accounting for a 
0.12% decrease.  
The Department states that it reviewed VGS’s supporting documentation and found that 
the annual base rate filing conforms with the Plan’s framework.  The Department reports that it 
“has identified no financial or procedural grounds necessitating an investigation under 30 V.S.A. 
§225.”  The Department recommends that the Commission allow the base rate adjustment to take 
effect as filed. 
 
After a detailed review of VGS’s proposed base rate adjustment and supporting 
documentation within the context of the Plan, we conclude that the proposed increase should 
take effect as filed.  
 
8 The Rate Smoothing Adjuster was a mechanism embedded in the Plan “to smooth the 2024 Base Rate Change 
by reducing FY2024 rates and creating a regulatory asset that will amortize over the term of the Plan and will be 
zero at the end of the Plan.”  Plan at Paragraph 3(b)(ii).  The Commission also examined the Rate Smoothing 
Adjuster in Case No. 23-0561-TF, which involved VGS’s most recent traditional cost-of-service rate case.

VGS calculated the formulaic adjustments as required by the Plan.  Because we conclude 
that VGS appropriately calculated its base rate adjustment consistent with the requirements of 
Paragraph 3 of the Plan, we approve VGS’s proposed 2027 annual base rate calculations for: (1) 
Operating Costs as adjusted by the Indexed Market Adjustment; and (2) Non-Operating Costs.     
V. 
CONCLUSION 
 
Based on our review of VGS’s filing and supporting materials as well as the 
Department’s recommendation, we conclude that the annual base rate filing conforms with the 
requirements of the Plan.  Therefore, we approve VGS’s tariff filing for a 0.61% increase in base 
rates, effective with bills rendered on or after November 1, 2026. 
 
  
 
SO ORDERED.
